title: Anatomical Resection of liver MetAstases iN patIents with RAS-mutated colorectal cancer
summary:
In recent years, important insights into the biology of colon cancer has been gained. It has become clear that colon cancer is not a uniform disease. Rather, there are different forms of colon cancer, which are caused in particular by the type of underlying altered genes in the tumor (so-called mutations). In this regard, there is increasing evidence from clinical studies that certain gene mutations (e.g., in the so-called RAS gene) significantly influence the response to therapies and should therefore be taken into account in the decision-making process of the therapy. While the consideration of mutations in the selection of chemotherapies is already widespread and applied, the choice of surgical therapy has so far been independent of this.
For the resection of liver metastases, there are two principal surgical techniques, which result from the structure of the liver from individual segments. In the so-called anatomical resection, the affected liver segment is almost completely removed. In non-anatomical resection, resection of the liver metastasis is performed with a sufficient safety margin, but independent of the boundaries of the affected segment.
The advantage of nonanatomic resection is the minimal loss of functional liver tissue. However, recent data from the USA show first indications that in patients with liver metastases from a colon cancer, anatomical resection is superior to non-anatomical resection in terms of disease-free survival if a specific mutation has been detected in the tumor (so-called RAS mutation). However, the available data are not sufficient to recommend anatomical resection as a standard technique in these patients. Therefore, these results need to be confirmed by a scientific high quality clinical study.
The aim of the ARMANI study is to evaluate whether anatomical resection of liver metastases prolongs disease-free survival in patients with colorectal cancer whose tumor has a mutation in the RAS gene compared to non-anatomical resection.

interventions.name: anatomical resection of liver metastases (almost complete removal of the affected liver segment)
non-anatomical resection of liver metastases (removal of the liver metastases with a sufficient safety margin, but independent of the borders of the affected segment)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• Colorectal cancer with RAS mutation (KRAS or NRAS)
• Colorectal liver metastases (single or multiple)
• Planned R0 resection of liver metastases (and primary tumor, if present)
• Anatomical and non-anatomical liver resection technically feasible 
• Male and female patients, age ≥ 18 years
• Written informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
• Extrahepatic metastases (Exceptions: patients with resectable, irradiable or ablatable extrahepatic metastases. Please note, that patients that are treated in palliative intention cannot participate in the study.)
• Planned staged liver resection (e.g. two-stage hepatectomy)
• Diagnosis of another cancer < 5 years prior to randomization Exceptions: curatively treated in situ cervical cancer, curatively resected non-melanoma skin cancer 
• Expected lack of compliance
• Addiction or other illnesses which do not allow the person concerned to assess the nature and extent of the clinical trial and its possible consequences
